segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ יָצָא שְׁמָהּ בָּעִיר ״מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת״ – הֲרֵי זוֹ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת; ״מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת״ – הֲרֵי זוֹ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת. וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שָׁם אֲמַתְלָא.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If «a rumor circulated in the city» that an unmarried woman is «betrothed, she is» considered to be «betrothed.» Similarly, if a rumor circulated that a married woman is «divorced, she is divorced, provided there is no» valid alternative «explanation [amatla]» for the rumor.

segments.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא אֲמַתְלָא? גֵּירַשׁ אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ עַל תְּנַאי; זָרַק לָהּ קִידּוּשֶׁיהָ – סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ, סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ – זוֹ הִיא אֲמַתְלָא.
segments.en: «What is» considered a valid «explanation?» For example, it is a case where there is a rumor that «so-and-so divorced his wife» but that the bill of divorce was given to her «conditionally.» It is therefore possible that the condition was not fulfilled and she is not actually divorced. Similarly, if there is a rumor that a woman was betrothed but that the man «threw her betrothal,» i.e., the money or document of betrothal, «to her,» and it is «uncertain» whether it was «closer to her» and «uncertain» whether it was «closer to him,» and therefore the status of their betrothal is likewise uncertain, «this is» considered a valid «explanation.»

moves.summary: A rumor of betrothal or divorce is effective, provided there is no amatla.

moves.cueHe: גירש איש פלוני את אשתו על תנאי
moves.summary: A conditional divorce, or a betrothal thrown equidistant between them.

positions.claim: a rumor that she is betrothed or divorced is effective absent an amatla such as a conditional get or doubtful betrothal throw
